articles.title: Sports-Focused Investment Firm Patricof Takes 8K SF at Marx’s 545 Madison Avenue
articles.narrative: Patricof, a private investment platform, has signed a 10-year lease for 7,500 square feet at Marx Realty's 545 Madison Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. The firm will occupy the entire 16th floor of the office building, relocating from its current address in the first quarter of 2027. Marx Realty's CEO noted that the building's distinctive design and hospitality-infused sensibility continue to attract high-quality tenants.

data_points.address: 545 Madison Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The building is also known as the Baccarat Building and features Baccarat crystals and luxury hotel-style finishes and amenities.

articles.title: Related Affiliate Nabs $167M From Greystone to Build Miami Resi Towers
articles.narrative: Related Urban Development Group, an affiliate of The Related Group, secured $167 million in construction financing from Greystone for the development of Gallery at Lummus Parc, a two-tower multifamily project in Miami. The financing package includes an $80 million construction loan from Greystone Housing Impact Investors and BlackRock Impact Opportunities Fund, along with $27.4 million in 4 percent Low-Income Housing Tax Credits from Greystone Real Estate Capital. This comprehensive financing solution, which also involves a Freddie Mac forward tax-exempt loan, will support the creation of 257 affordable and workforce housing units in downtown Miami, with completion expected in late 2028.

data_points.notable_features: Two interconnected towers of 30 and 27 stories, with approximately 83% of units designated as affordable housing ranging from 20% to 100% of area median income. Amenities include coworking spaces, a health club, a rooftop pool, grilling areas, a pickleball court, and an outdoor fitness area. The project benefits from close access to public transportation.
data_points.project_notes: The financing includes an $80 million construction loan and $27.4 million in 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC). Greystone also obtained a Freddie Mac forward tax-exempt loan to repay construction financing costs with LIHTC equity, providing a clear path to long-term permanent financing.

articles.title: In Manhattan Investment Sales, the Money Is Moving Faster Than the Market
articles.narrative: Manhattan's commercial real estate investment sales market is experiencing a nuanced recovery, with dollar volume increasing but transaction velocity remaining below historical averages. While most property sectors, including office, retail, land, hotels, and free-market apartments, show positive momentum and strong fundamentals, the rent-regulated multifamily sector continues to struggle due to frozen rent increases and rising operating costs. The author argues that while more capital is flowing into the market, the number of properties changing hands has not yet returned to pre-pandemic or long-term average levels, indicating that the 'money is moving faster than the market.' A true recovery, according to the author, will be marked by a significant increase in the number of properties sold, not just larger transaction sizes.

articles.title: Venn Acquires Leasing Agent Company Zuma for $50M
articles.narrative: Multifamily operating platform Venn has acquired Zuma, a leasing company specializing in agentic artificial intelligence, for $50 million. This acquisition enhances Venn's capabilities in leasing, renewals, and collections by integrating Zuma's deep expertise in AI-driven leasing solutions. The deal brings Zuma's co-founders, Shiv Gettu and Kendrick Bradley, into Venn's leadership, with Gettu overseeing strategic partnerships and Bradley leading the company's leasing practice.

articles.title: Westlight Capital Founder Doug Faron On Going Long in Multifamily
articles.narrative: Doug Faron, founder of Westlight Capital, discusses his career trajectory from investment banking to leading two entrepreneurial real estate investment firms. He highlights his experience at CIM Group, where he oversaw $10 billion in real estate investments, and the strategic shift from Shoreham Capital's build-to-rent focus to Westlight Capital's broader multifamily mandate. Faron emphasizes the importance of relationships in fundraising and adapting investment strategies to changing market conditions, such as the move from developing build-to-rent projects to acquiring existing multifamily assets when cap rates shifted.

articles.title: Partnership to Develop 225,000 SF Office Project in Allen, Texas
articles.narrative: KDC and Pillar Commercial have formed a partnership to develop One Bethany North, a 225,000-square-foot office project in Allen, Texas. The nine-story building will be part of the Watters Creek mixed-use development and will feature various amenities including pickleball courts, putting greens, and a restaurant.

data_points.notable_features: Located within the Watters Creek mixed-use development, with amenities including pickleball courts, putting greens, outdoor gathering spaces, and a 3,500-square-foot restaurant.

articles.title: 37th Parallel Acquires 222-Unit Apartment Complex in Sachse, Texas
articles.narrative: 37th Parallel Properties, a Virginia-based investment firm, has acquired Woodbridge Villas, a 222-unit apartment complex in Sachse, a northeastern suburb of Dallas. The property, built in 2002, features a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units with an average size of 875 square feet. The seller and sales price were not disclosed.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, fitness center, clubhouse, business center, outdoor grilling and dining stations, and a pet park.

articles.title: JLL Negotiates Sale of Shopping Center in Northwest Austin
articles.narrative: JLL has facilitated the sale of Casis Village, a shopping center located in the Tarrytown neighborhood of northwest Austin. The property, anchored by a prominent grocer and 92% leased at the time of sale, was acquired by an undisclosed buyer from a joint venture between Ivy Cos. and 35 South Capital.

articles.title: Wells Fargo Signs 20,560 SF Office Lease Renewal in Southwest Austin
articles.narrative: Wells Fargo has renewed its 20,560-square-foot office lease within Building I at Uplands Corporate Center in southwest Austin. JLL represented the tenant, while Cushman & Wakefield represented the landlord, Drawbridge Realty, in the transaction.

articles.title: PCCP Provides $66.8M Construction Loan for Northern New Jersey Multifamily Project
articles.narrative: PCCP LLC has provided a $66.8 million senior construction loan for Plaza Greene, a 145-unit multifamily project in Fair Lawn, New Jersey. The development, a partnership between Sterling Properties and Danbro Properties, will include age-restricted residences with 12 percent designated as affordable housing. A Sprouts Farmers Market will anchor the ground-floor retail space.

data_points.address: 21-01 Fair Lawn Ave, Fair Lawn, NJ
data_points.notable_features: Age-restricted residences; 12% of units reserved as affordable housing; amenities include fitness center, spa, and landscaped courtyard.

articles.title: CBRE’s Dallas office adds vice chair, industrial specialist
articles.narrative: Ward Richmond has joined CBRE's Dallas office as a Vice Chair within its Industrial & Logistics Occupier Leasing team, bringing over two decades of experience in advising industrial occupiers on real estate portfolio and supply chain optimization across North America. He is joined by his former team from Colliers, including Cole Hooper, James Ewing, Amanda Richards, and Keller Strauss. The team's collective experience includes 382 transactions since 2020, totaling over 43 million square feet and approximately $1.6 billion in value, demonstrating their strong client relationships and expertise in the industrial sector.

articles.title: JLL provides $406 million in financing for Dallas’ Trammel Crow Center
articles.narrative: JLL's Capital Markets group has secured $406 million in five-year, fixed-rate financing for the Trammell Crow Center, a prominent 1.2 million-square-foot trophy office tower in Dallas' Arts District. The loan, provided by Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley, was arranged on behalf of the borrower, Regent Properties, LLC. The 50-story property, which underwent a significant $182 million renovation in 2019, is 92% leased to a strong tenant mix and offers Class AA amenities and a prime location within the largest contiguous urban arts district in the United States.

data_points.notable_features: 50-story trophy office tower located in the Dallas Arts District, overlooking Klyde Warren Park and the Nasher Sculpture Center, with a competitive 3.0 per 1,000 square feet parking ratio and a full suite of Class AA amenities.
data_points.project_notes: The property benefited from a transformative $182 million renovation completed in 2019 by prior ownership, which included a new parking structure, ground-floor retail, lobby renovation, and amenity upgrades.

articles.market_intelligence: The 118-acre Dallas Arts District is the largest contiguous urban arts district in the United States, attracting over 1.5 million visitors annually and generating an estimated $400 million in economic impact.

articles.title: Daniel Management Group awarded new apartment assignment in Mundelein
articles.narrative: Daniel Management Group (DMG) has been awarded the management assignment for Lakeside Village Apartments in Mundelein, Illinois, expanding its partnership with Hawthorne Management Services. The 144-unit multifamily community features newly renovated units and a range of amenities, situated near Diamond Lake, Hawthorne Mall, and a METRA station. DMG will oversee a rebrand, clubhouse upgrades, outdoor area improvements, ongoing unit renovations, and a new website for the property.

data_points.notable_features: Newly renovated units with high-end finishes, pet-friendly, and amenities including a clubhouse, picnic area, playground, and onsite management. Located near Diamond Lake, Hawthorne Mall, and a METRA station.
data_points.project_notes: Daniel Management Group will conduct a rebrand, upgrade the clubhouse and outdoor areas, oversee ongoing unit renovations, and launch a new website.

articles.title: Lee & Associates closes 10,500-square-foot industrial lease in Fort Worth
articles.narrative: Lee & Associates Dallas-Fort Worth has facilitated a new industrial lease for a 10,500-square-foot service facility in Fort Worth, Texas. The tenant, Paragon Pro Rentals, secured the space at IndustriParks820 Lot 1, with Lee & Associates representing both the tenant and the landlord, CanTex Capital.

data_points.address: 5701 Parker Henderson Road, Fort Worth, TX

articles.title: Nine Options: Shallow bay supply runs dry
articles.narrative: Chicago's industrial market is experiencing a severe shortage of shallow bay industrial space, particularly for tenants needing 15,000 to 50,000 square feet. This scarcity is driving significant pricing pressure and lease activity in the smaller size ranges, even as overall industrial leasing volume saw a slight dip in Q2 2026. While big box leases contribute to the overall square footage, shallow bay occupiers are responsible for the high deal count, with construction and building materials companies being a primary driver. The limited new construction pipeline for shallow bay facilities, coupled with higher per-square-foot development costs compared to larger bulk warehouses, means that relief for tenants is not imminent, leading to 'sticker shock' at renewal for many.

people.name: Packy Doyle
people.title: Executive Vice President of Industrial Services

articles.market_intelligence: Chicago's industrial market saw 153 leases signed in Q2 2026, with 79 of those between 20,000 and 100,000 square feet, totaling 3.7 million square feet. Overall leasing volume was 10.6 million square feet, down from 14.4 million in Q1 but marking the fourth consecutive quarter above 10 million. Vacancy decreased by 20 basis points to 4.5%, and net absorption reached 5.8 million square feet, significantly higher than 648,700 square feet a year prior. Average asking rent hit $8.12 per square foot. Only 232,600 square feet of speculative shallow bay space broke ground in Q2, bringing the total pipeline to 740,700 square feet across nine buildings.

articles.title: Rental Condos Debut in N. Miami
articles.narrative: Fortune International Group and Blue Road have delivered Nexo Residences, a 16-story short-term rental condominium project in North Miami Beach. The development, built by KAST Construction, features 254 fully furnished units ranging from studios to three-bedroom floorplans, as well as three- and four-bedroom townhomes. Owners will benefit from rental flexibility managed by AvantStay, a hospitality management company, with an on-site team handling guest services.

data_points.address: 13899 Biscayne Blvd., North Miami Beach, FL
data_points.notable_features: Units are delivered fully furnished and offer short-term rental flexibility; amenities include a tech hub with coworking spaces, a luxury pool deck, fitness center, and a rooftop observatory deck.

articles.title: Orion Acquires 88K-SF Boone Retail Center
articles.narrative: Orion Real Estate Group has acquired Watauga Village, an 88,800-square-foot, Food Lion-anchored neighborhood shopping center in Boone, North Carolina, for $26.1 million. This acquisition marks Orion's first shopping center in the state, expanding its portfolio beyond single-tenant, triple-net properties. The fully leased center benefits from its strategic location in Boone's commercial hub, near Appalachian State University and a regional medical center.

data_points.notable_features: Food Lion-anchored neighborhood shopping center, shadow-anchored by a Walmart Supercenter, and adjacent to Watauga Medical Center. Located in the commercial center of Boone, home to Appalachian State University.

articles.title: PTM Lands $125M Financing for St. Pete Multifamily Community
articles.narrative: PTM Partners secured a $125 million construction loan from GID for EDGE Collective II, a 330-unit multifamily high-rise with retail space in St. Petersburg's EDGE District. Berkadia arranged the three-year, floating-rate financing for the Class AA project. This second phase builds upon the success of the initial phase, which included a hotel and other mixed-use components.

data_points.notable_features: Class AA multifamily high-rise with ground-floor retail.
data_points.project_notes: This is Phase II of the EDGE Collective development.

articles.title: JV Pays $220M for Alpharetta Hotel
articles.narrative: A joint venture between Endeavor Real Estate Group and Cox has acquired The Hotel at Avalon, a 330-key hotel in Alpharetta, from Crescent Real Estate for $220 million. The hotel, which opened in 2018, is part of the larger Avalon mixed-use district and includes the Alpharetta Conference Center.

data_points.notable_features: Features a second-floor swimming pool, fitness center, on-site restaurant, event venues, and 407 parking spaces. Includes the 65,000-square-foot Alpharetta Conference Center with 44,000 square feet of flexible meeting space.
data_points.project_notes: Located within the $1 billion, 86-acre Avalon mixed-use district.

articles.title: KKR, Mirastar Acquire Eight UK Logistics Properties from Ares
articles.narrative: KKR and its European industrial and logistics platform, Mirastar, have acquired a portfolio of eight fully occupied logistics properties across the UK from Ares Real Estate funds. The 2.7-million-square-foot portfolio, valued at approximately $529 million, includes modern assets in established distribution markets such as the Midlands, South East, and North of England. KKR noted the strong fundamentals in the UK logistics sector, driven by robust occupier demand and limited supply, making this acquisition an attractive opportunity for durable income and growth.

data_points.notable_features: Modern, high-quality assets with strong connectivity to key population centers and transportation infrastructure.

articles.title: Newsom Signs Bills Aimed At Cold Storage Post-Boyle Heights Fire
articles.narrative: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed two bills into law that aim to improve safety regulations for cold storage facilities, following a significant fire at a Boyle Heights cold storage plant. The legislation, initially limited in scope, will expand to a statewide application in 2028. These measures are intended to prevent future incidents and enhance the safety standards of such industrial properties.

articles.title: Maricopa County Data Center Project Moves Toward Approval Despite Pushback
articles.narrative: The Glendale Planning Commission has recommended rezoning approval for Project Baccara, a proposed data center campus, despite local opposition. This decision advances the project to the city council for final consideration.

articles.title: Robotaxi Firms Quietly Growing Real Estate Footprint, Even Where They're Not Yet Legal
articles.narrative: Robotaxi companies are significantly expanding their real estate footprint, with leased space in 2026 already surpassing the cumulative total from the previous four years. This growth indicates a strategic move to establish operational hubs and infrastructure, even in markets where autonomous vehicle services are not yet fully legal. The expansion suggests these firms are preparing for future widespread deployment and scaling of their services.

articles.title: Moishe Mana Drops $89M On Fort Lauderdale Office: The South Florida Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: Moishe Mana has acquired an office building in Fort Lauderdale, marking his initial investment in Broward County. The transaction was valued at $89 million.

articles.title: Hotel Industry Sees Record-High Increases In RevPAR, ADR
articles.narrative: The U.S. hotel industry is experiencing a widespread recovery, marked by significant year-over-year increases in both revenue per available room (RevPAR) and average daily rate (ADR). This positive trend indicates a robust rebound in demand and pricing power across the sector.
